summary: Ventura County lookout on Triunfo Peak, first staffed 1930, moved here from Bodle Peak in 1934-35; gone by the late 1960s, with a concrete base remaining.

facts.design: 60-foot X-brace steel tower with an 8x8 observation cabin
facts.status_note: Tower gone after the late 1960s; register says a concrete base of unknown purpose remains and the area burned in the 2018 Woolsey Fire

access.note: Hiking trail from the Backbone Trail via Yellow Hill Fire Road, per a hiker's undated account; within the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area

visit.trail_note: From the Backbone Trail, a side trail reaches Yellow Hill Fire Road, the old lookout service road; about three-quarters of a mile to the top

events.note: First lookout station put up with Ventura County help; telephone service completed June 1930
Jack Fletcher was the lookout when fire leapt up the frame tower, October 31, 1930
Register says the November 1930 Potrero fire incinerated the tower; Los Angeles County rebuilt it
Tower dismantled at Bodle Peak and re-erected at Triunfo Peak
Los Angeles County annual report: a lookout tower was constructed on Triunfo Peak; hiking blog also dates reassembly to 1935
Newspaper report of a fire that burned out of control all night behind the Triunfo Lookout Station
A house fire on the Huston ranch was discovered from the Triunfo lookout station

corrections.proposed: Removed in the late 1960s (no exact year in sources)
corrections.why: The register field reads 'Late 1960's'. The brief's 1960 has no source, and the hiking blog also says the late 1960s.

corrections.proposed: First station 1930; tower moved from Bodle Peak and re-erected at Triunfo 1934-1935
corrections.why: A June 1930 newspaper quoted on the Forest Lookouts page shows the station in service by 1930. 1934 is when the Bodle Peak tower was re-erected here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and a November 1934 newspaper item put the move in 1934. A 1935 county annual report and a hiking blog say 1935.
A newspaper dated October 31, 1930 says fire leapt up the frame tower. The register dates the incineration to the November 1930 Potrero fire. The sources do not say whether these are one fire.
The register and the 1934 newspaper item say 60 feet. A 1955 newspaper item says 80-foot steel tower. The brief's 18.3 m follows the 60-foot figure.

notes_for_editor: Gone lookout; the brief's 'built 1934' and 'removed 1960' were both incomplete. The station dates from 1930, and removal is late 1960s with no exact year. Today's condition rests on the register's photo caption and a satellite-image description; no source describes the site after the 2018 fire. Access 'public' is from a hiker's undated account and the Santa Monica Mountains NRA location, not a rule.
